events.text: Dawn on September 28, 1835. Your family has turned off the road near Liberty with its two wagons, an ox to each, and the horse, towards land of its own.
Your family rolled a 13, and a 16 for what it has.

The family has reached its own land. There is no house yet, so they camp by the wagon. They unload what they brought: 6 × barrel of meal and salt meat, 6 × sack of seed, 6 × powder and lead, hoe, felling axe, bedding and iron pot. A labor of land, 177 acres, is marked out for the family. No title has been issued. The wagon stands at the surveyor's mark. Choose where the house will stand.

The family has chosen where the house will stand. The house will stand in the timber, 2 feet above Big Bayou. Water that runs all year is close by at Big Bayou. It is low ground in the river bottom, and the river comes over it in a flood. The lane to the road will be 0.3 miles.
The wagon is drawn up where the house will stand, and the family makes camp beside it and puts up the tent.
Son 2 hh-4, Daughter 3 hh-4 and Son 4 hh-4 have nothing to do, and have gone to find Mother 1 hh-4.
Mother 1 hh-4 has stopped the work about the place to talk with Son 2 hh-4, Daughter 3 hh-4 and Son 4 hh-4, who have nothing to do. Give them something to do and Mother 1 hh-4 goes back to it.
Son 2 hh-4 set out: keep house.
Son 2 hh-4 has something to do now, and Mother 1 hh-4 goes back to the work about the place.

Son 2 hh-4 finished: keep house.

Concepción Mora reined in on the road and spoke with Son 4 hh-4.

Concepción Mora: “I've come from Liberty, and I did not see any of this myself. Ada Swinney put it in my hands there, and had it from another rider before that, out of Gonzales. There are Mexican soldiers on the far bank of the Guadalupe, across from the town. They came for the cannon, and the town has told them no.”
A Mexican detachment has reached the Guadalupe opposite Gonzales to reclaim the cannon. Local settlers have refused to return it.
An express from San Felipe has reached the Trinity with word that the Mexican troops are at Gonzales and the settlements are turning out. Does somebody from your family ride west to join them?

Mother 1 hh-4 rode the range and counted the stock and brought in one cow that had strayed: 6 cattle and 15 hogs, the cattle fair, the hogs fair. The calves are marked, and nothing will stray for a month.
Concepción Mora would wait no longer and rode on. Nothing further was asked.
Mother 1 hh-4 finished: ride the range after the stock.

There was a fight at the Mexican camp, and it was short. The soldiers have gone back toward Béxar, and the cannon did not go with them.”
Mexican detachment withdraws; Texians retain the cannon.

Word has come of a fight at Mission Concepción on the morning of the 28th. About ninety men under Bowie and Fannin, surrounded in the fog, beat back the Mexican cavalry and infantry and took a cannon. Richard Andrews of Mina was killed. How many of the Mexican soldiers fell, the reports do not agree: sixteen dead were counted on the field, and others say fifty, sixty-seven, or more.
